messages:
mike: ran a quick nsys skyline on the 2k-token steady-state workload, attaching top-level findings
sri: can you paste the top kernels? small snippet is fine
mike: Top kernels by total GPU time (summary from nsys):
  1) fused_attn_forward_kernel — 42.1% total time
  2) kv_cache_lookup_loop — 18.7%
  3) kv_prefetch_dispatch — 9.3%
  4) gelu_fast_player — 5.6%
  5) softmax_blocked — 4.9%
  (rest <4%)
devon: interesting that fused_attn is >40% — expected, but the kv_lookup is higher than before. did you use batch_size=8?
mike: yep bs=8, seq=2048, model=rwkv-derived, quant=4bit. Also saw lots of small dynamic kernel launches around KV paths in the timeline (spiky).
perf-bot: analysis note: timeline shows high launch overheads at ~1.8s intervals correlated with cache misses (see perfetto markers)
katie: do we have occupancy/SM util numbers for fused_attn? could be underutilized warps or shared mem throttle
mike: fused_attn occupancy ~45% (SM util ~72%) but warp scheduler stalls dominated by 'sync' and 'mem_throttle' events. NVPROF stack shows a lot of time in memcpy (host->device) around prefetch windows.
sri: that suggests we're doing synchronous prefetching that blocks compute. Are we prefetching per-request rather than batched across the queue?
mike: yes — current heuristic fires prefetch on request start. If requests arrive spread, prefetches race and evict KV entries. I instrumented KV cache eviction count: evicts/sec ~ 4200 vs baseline 900.
devon: huge. That would explain kv_cache_lookup loop time increase (re-populating cache). Could also be causing small kernels (kv_prefetch_dispatch) to be launched a lot.
katie: can we try deferred prefetch: accumulate requests for 2ms and issue a single prefetch/xfer for that batch? simulation?
mike: simulated in python harness: coalescing 2ms reduces prefetch launches by ~6x and predicted GPU time for kv_prefetch path drops 70%. But latency tail worsens slightly for cold keys (p99 +12ms).
sri: tradeoff sounds worth for throughput SLO, but for p99-sensitive routes we need hybrid: immediate prefetch for pinned/high-priority requests, coalesced for best-effort.
devon: from kernel-selection POV, the fused_attn still dominates. We should check if kernel selector picks a different kernel variant for shorter seq lengths — maybe it's selecting a variant with more shared memory usage causing mem_throttle.
mike: good call. I dumped selector decisions for the trace: for layer 3..23 it picks 'attn_shared_opt' everywhere. That variant uses 2-block shared tile causing bank conflicts on Ampere gen when seq>1024.
katie: so combined issue: (1) KV prefetch storms decreasing cache hit rate -> more KV loops and small kernel overhead, (2) attn variant causing bank conflicts -> stalls. Two levers.
sri: prioritize fixes: 1) change prefetch heuristic to coalesced by default + exception for high-priority; 2) add fallback kernel variant 'attn_no_shared' for seq>1024 or ampere hardware.
mike: I'll open a PR with the prefetch change and a perf test. patch will also expose a selector metric to console. drafting notes: `prefetch.window_ms=2`, `prefetch.mode=coalesce|immediate` and `selector.fallback_on_conflicts=true`.
devon: can you also attach the small perfetto flame screenshot? helps with SRE review.
mike: attached -> perfetto link: https://perfetto/reports/abc123 (internal)
katie: after PR we should run a regression matrix: bs {1,4,8,16} x seq {256,1024,2048} on Ampere + Hopper, measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel breakdown.
sri: also add a synthetic that forces KV cold path to validate eviction numbers.
mike: will run overnight and post results tomorrow morning :thumbsup:
